doc.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: No racial problem if you acknowledge God
summary: Hendricks says there is only mankind and that talking about race is the problem.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: preacher said, “well you know I do.” And my father said, “well then what’s your problem?” And the rocking kept on. And not another word was spoken. And I said whooooh. He got right to the heart of the matter. Because that’s the key. We still talk about a problem. There is no problem. There is no racial problem if you acknowledge God. Because if you acknowledge God then you are looking at another child of God. So what are you talking about? If you’re going to separate from that other child of God because of this mythical term you have here, you are acting in an ungodly way. So when people ask me about race, I say, “what time does it start?”

Well you know there is no such thing — there is just mankind, that’s all there is on this planet. You will only find mankind, that’s it, that’s the highest form of life you’re going to find here. And He looks like every type of thing you can imagine. In every part of the world He looks different. But He eats the same foods. And He has a way of wrapping the meat in some kind of a dough, that’s called a tortilla or a blintz or a crepe. But it’s still wrapping meat in dough. Every where you go He does this.
He had a big box of crayons.

Exactly. This is ridiculous, this paying attention to this problem. I believe if you talk about the problem you are the problem. And you see these well meaning people I’m sure, talking about race, they are the problem. Because they have separated man from man, and now they’re going to solve the way to try to get them back together. First they’ve separated them with their own voices in their own words, and then they’re going to try to get them back together? How are they going to do that? They create an insolvable problem, when all they have to do is treat everybody like they would want to be treated themselves. Just like Christ and everybody else said — and then they’ll be the first to tell you, “oh it’s very complex.” It’s complex because they have this evil in their heart that they have no intention of getting rid of. That’s the complexity. It’s not complex. It’s simple.
You know I wish we could clone you.
Send in the clones. Forgive me.
I set it up, you picked up.
I can’t resist a straight line.
